title: Restriction-transpose resolution model for the specified comparison mate
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete commutative ring. Use small representatives of the small etale and pro-etale sites in a common larger universe [def-weil-size-convention], with their constant-$\Lambda$ module categories and bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $Q$ for localization of complexes, $A_T=\nu_T^*$ for exact comparison inverse image, and $N_T=\nu_{T,*}$ for its right adjoint [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact].
Let $u:U\to V$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $F$ a $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, and $i:F[0]\to I$, $t:A_UI\to J$ quasi-isomorphisms with $I,J$ nonnegative, termwise injective K-injective complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Put $h=\operatorname{adj}(t):I\to N_UJ$, $C=u_{\mathrm{et},*}I$, and $D=u_{\mathrm{proet},*}J$, using the ordinary module direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $\delta:N_Vu_{\mathrm{proet},*}\xrightarrow{\sim}u_{\mathrm{et},*}N_U$ be the restriction identity: on each etale $W/V$ both sides evaluate a pro-etale sheaf $G$ as $G(W\times_VU)$, with its restriction maps and coefficient action. Set $k=\delta_J^{-1}\circ u_{\mathrm{et},*}(h):C\to N_VD$ and let $d:A_VC\to D$ be its adjunction transpose [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].
Then, under the canonical resolution identifications $QC\cong Ru_{\mathrm{et},*}F$ and $QD\cong Ru_{\mathrm{proet},*}A_UF$ (the latter induced by $t\circ A_U(i)$), $Qd$ is the specified comparison $b_{u,F}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. More explicitly, writing $l=u_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$ for the etale module inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], $p=u_{\mathrm{proet}}^*$ and $\varepsilon^e,\varepsilon^p$ for their ordinary adjunction counits, and $a^0:A_Ul\xrightarrow{\sim}pA_V$ for the canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], one has the chain-map equality
$$\varepsilon^p_J\circ p(d)\circ a^0_C=t\circ A_U(\varepsilon^e_I).$$
Consequently its derived transpose is exactly $A_U(\varepsilon^e_{u,F})\circ a_{u,Ru_{\mathrm{et},*}F}^{-1}$ with the specified derived counit and pullback comparison. In every degree and for every terminal section $z$ of $C$, $k(z)=h(z)$ as a section of $J$ on $U$, and $d(A_V(z))=h(z)$. Here comparison pullback of a section uses the canonical constant-ring unit identification. No preservation of injective objects by $A_U$ or $A_V$ is assumed.

proof.text: Let e be the canonical ordinary direct-image comparison lowerStarComparisonUpperStarBaseChange. The comparison adjunction unit equation unit_mateEquiv_symm and naturality of the restriction isomorphism show, degree by degree, d = e_I followed by the direct image of t. This is equality of chain maps, not just homotopy classes. All maps are the specified ones, and no replacements are changed.

source.place: Tag 0B65, mate correspondence and unit normalization; naturality calculation with t.

proof.text: The iterated-mate/conjugate equation identifies the mate of e under the two morphism inverse-image adjunctions with the specified pullback comparison. Its counit equation gives a0 followed by p(e_I) and the pro-etale counit equal to A_U of the etale counit. Postcompose with t, and apply naturality of the pro-etale counit. Using the chain-map factorization in the preceding step gives the asserted chain identity.

source.place: Tags 0B65 and 0DV0; iterated mates and the counit equations.

proof.text: Compute the right-derived base-change transformation on the supplied augmented injective resolutions using its defining factorization with the right-derived units. Naturality of the unit along t identifies Q(r_proet(t)) followed by the unit on J with the unit on A_U I followed by Rr_proet(Qt). Cancel the unit on I, which is invertible because I is bounded below with injective terms. Naturality of the exact-localization factor along i identifies the product of the factor on I, Qt, the inverse of Q(A_U(i) followed by t), and the inverse factor on F[0] with the inverse of A_U(Qi). Naturality of derived base change along Qi then cancels this inverse. The resulting equation is exactly the stated comparisonResolutionDerivedMap equals fixedComparisonDirectImageMatePlus: the resolution identifications are their prescribed derived-unit and inverse-augmentation constructions. The calculation is proved as the private generic baseChange_resolutions lemma. It uses neither preservation of injectives by comparison inverse image nor an independently chosen derived adjunction.

source.place: Tags 015F and 0FND, exact functor localization and canonical derived comparison; implemented by the proved library rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange_fac and right-derived-unit naturality.

proof.text: Replace the derived resolution map by the fixed comparison just computed. Its specified counit normalization, after cancelling the pullback comparison isomorphism, gives exactly the displayed derived transpose equation.

At any degree, the inverse restriction comparison evaluates at the terminal etale object as the identity: its base-change isomorphism is componentwise identity and a presheaf maps an identity to an identity. Thus k(z)=h(z). Evaluate the comparison adjunction identity homEquiv(homEquiv.symm(k))=k at that degree and terminal section to obtain d(A_V(z))=k(z). Combining the two equations gives both required section identities without any cocycle restriction.

Suggest adding the normalization to the comparison-pullback statement. Step 3: I re-derived both transposes, r(h) and k, and injectivity gives the chain identity. No preservation of injectives is assumed. Step 5: checked against the lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general formula with s=i,f=id_C and s=j,f=d, the exact left adjoint taken without replacement; this is the same use accepted in canonical-mate step 9. Step 6: I redid the cancellation; it gives adj_p(B)=q_{u,F}, so B=b_{u,F}. It is not circular. Step 7: the terminal-section evaluation is correct. Edge cases U empty, Lambda=0 and u=id are consistent. The proof-dependency closure (505 nodes) does not reach the item or its parent, so there is no cycle, and no SGA is used.
